transcript.content: Hello. I am Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Thank you so much for taking the time to see me today. I really appreciate it. 

Um, well, I guess I'm here because I've been having a little bit of trouble at work lately. It's probably nothing major, and I feel a little silly even bringing it up, honestly, but I just want to make sure I'm doing my best, you know? 

It's just that I can't seem to keep my mind on a task long enough to finish it anymore. Even when it's really important. Like, I do computer support, and I'll start tracing a client's network problem... and maybe ten minutes later I'll realize I've just reread the exact same log entries three times, and I still don't actually know what they say. 

I'm sure everyone gets a little distracted sometimes, but it's been bothering me. I hope I'm explaining that okay—is that the sort of thing you were asking about?
Have you experienced these kinds of difficulties with focus and concentration throughout your life, or is this a relatively new problem for you?

Well, um, I guess it's not entirely new. I mean, I've always been a little energetic, maybe a bit scattered. My mother actually still jokes about it. She likes to remind me that back in grade school, my report cards always said I was bright—which is nice of her to remember—but, um, they also usually said I had a hard time staying in my seat. And that I'd kind of blurt out answers before the teacher finished asking. 

I also had this terrible habit of losing my homework, even when I had actually done it, which was always so frustrating. But kids are just like that sometimes, right? Full of energy and a little disorganized? I always just figured it was a normal phase, or just my personality. I hope that makes sense. Is that the kind of background you were looking for?
Beyond the trouble with focus, have you been feeling down, depressed, or lacking interest in things you usually enjoy lately?

No, no, nothing like that. I mean, I'm generally a pretty upbeat guy, I think. I definitely still enjoy my hobbies—I love tinkering with electronics and going for bike rides when the weather's nice. 

I don't feel sad or down or anything. It's really just the... the frustration of not getting my work done as well as I know I can. I really try to keep a positive attitude about it, though. I'm sorry if I gave the impression I was depressed, I definitely didn't mean to. Does that answer your question okay?

Aside from the frustration regarding your work performance, do you find yourself frequently worrying about many different things in your daily life, such as your health, finances, or the safety of your loved ones?

Oh, no, not at all. I mean, I guess I think about normal everyday things, like making sure the bills are paid, but I definitely don't sit around worrying about them. I'm actually pretty lucky that way, I think. I just try to take things as they come, you know? 

I really don't stress too much about my health or finances or anything like that. I hope that's a good thing? I mean, I know it's important to be responsible, but I really try not to let things weigh on me too much. Did I answer that right, or did you mean a different kind of worry?
Do you still find yourself feeling restless or having the urge to move around when you are expected to stay seated, such as during meetings or while working at your desk?

Well, um... maybe a little? I really try to be professional and respectful, especially in meetings, so I hope it doesn't come across as rude to my colleagues. But... yeah, if I'm being totally honest, even when I'm supposed to just sit still and listen, it kind of feels like there's this... this motor humming under my skin. 

It's a little embarrassing to admit, but it's like I just have this intense urge to stand up, check something, or just move on to the next problem right that exact second. I usually try to hide it by just shifting my weight or maybe tapping my pen quietly so I don't disrupt anyone else. I really hope that doesn't make me sound like a bad listener or a bad employee. Did I explain that okay, or is that not what you were asking about?
Has this difficulty with focus and the urge to move around caused you to receive any formal feedback, warnings, or negative evaluations from your supervisor at work?

Well... I mean, I really pride myself on being a hard worker, I do. But, um... since I lost the structure of my old job and started doing more freelance and contract work, it's... it's been a bit of a struggle, if I'm being perfectly honest. 

I haven't really gotten, like, a formal write-up or anything like that. It's more... well, my reputation has taken a bit of a hit, I think. I've actually lost a few freelance clients recently because I just... I couldn't seem to get things finished when I said I would. And, um, I was actually up for a senior service-manager role a little while ago, and I missed out on it. I think people just... they don't quite trust me to follow through on things right now. 

It's really embarrassing to admit, and it's actually caused some financial stress for me and my wife, which I feel terrible about. I really want to be reliable, I just... I keep dropping the ball. I hope you don't think less of me for that. I'm really trying my best to fix it. Is that... does that answer what you were asking about work?
Do you find that these challenges with staying on task and the urge to move around also impact your personal life or household responsibilities, such as managing chores or paying bills on time?

Well, I really do try to stay on top of things, I promise. I want to be dependable, so I hope it doesn't sound like I'm just completely careless. But... um... yeah, if I'm being totally honest, it does spill over a bit. 

It's mostly that I just... I end up forgetting these really ordinary but important things. Like, I'll completely forget to return a client's call, or I'll realize too late that I missed paying the cloud backup bill. Or, um, I teach this volunteer class sometimes, and I'll show up and realize I forgot to bring the right adapter. 

It's really embarrassing. I usually end up spending the whole next day just apologizing to everyone and trying to patch up the damage. I feel awful when I let people down like that, because I really do care. I'm trying my absolute best to keep track of it all, I really am. I hope that makes sense? Did I answer what you were looking for there?
